# Every mechanism the mixed-era matrix names, one stanza each:
#
#   mechanism   <name>
#   witness     <process|wire|peer> <the one function that may file that
#                 mechanism's evidence of that class>
#   era         <era> claimed|absent
#   entailed-by <era> <mechanism>  (optional, repeatable per era)
#   proposition <the exact claim the name denotes>
#
# Five things are frozen here, and the run refuses whatever it is handed that
# disagrees with each:
#
#   the proposition — each era's declared conformance quotes its mechanism's
#     proposition back, and the manifest refuses a declaration whose text
#     differs by a byte, so the two eras' columns cannot come to answer
#     different questions. The freeze binds the declaration — a string the
#     harness hands the manifest — and nothing here binds that string to a
#     peer process;
#   the name — no name twice, and no two names carrying one proposition, so a
#     name cannot be aimed at what another name already denotes;
#   the disposition — a declaration claiming an era this file calls absent, or
#     one declaring an absence for an era it calls claimed, is refused, so
#     dropping a declared absence to turn an UNPROVEN row PROVEN is an edit
#     here;
#   the witness — a fact reaches the journal only from the site named for its
#     mechanism and class, so an observation one witness already made cannot be
#     filed a second time under another mechanism's name;
#   the entailment — a row carried on another row's artifact rather than on one
#     of its own is refused unless an "entailed-by" line above declares that
#     exact pair, for that era, between two rows this file disposes of the same
#     way. A mechanism naming no witness is redeemable by entailment alone, and
#     one naming no entailment cannot be carried at all.
#
# A proposition is exactly what its witness observes, no wider: a clause the
# matrix never checks makes a PROVEN cell mean less than it reads.
#
# WHAT THE COMPILER REFUSES
#
#   Everything this gate's verdict is made of lives in package
#   ci/mixedera/coverage, and the harness in ci/mixedera imports that package
#   rather than declaring it. None of that state is exported: not the coverage
#   row a release is gated on, not the ledger of which observations happened,
#   not the evidence journal, not the map of eras a record is rendered from, not
#   the seal over these frozen files. So none of this compiles, from a case body
#   or from anywhere else in the harness:
#
#     writing a row redeemed — the redemption verb decides, against the journal;
#     marking a claim observed — a case marks its own line and nothing else, and
#       a claim's line is marked only by the redemption that earned it, so a
#       case emptied to bookkeeping reports nothing;
#     dropping an era from the manifest — its rows and its era map are
#       unexported; and a manifest built without every era this file disposes
#       of is refused before the matrix runs, so no record is left with
#       nothing in it to refuse;
#     appending to the evidence journal — the two observers are the only way in,
#       and the witness binding runs inside them;
#     writing the sealed text — and a second Bind is refused — so a later read
#       cannot be given a different file than the run started on.
#
#   Those five are the moves that cleared this gate as it stood before this
#   pass, each one a line or two of state assignment inside a case body. As
#   they were written, each is a compile error now rather than a finding for
#   an audit.
#
# WHAT THIS TEXT STILL BINDS
#
#   the five freezes above — proposition, name, disposition, witness,
#     entailment — read back out of this file on every single read, so nothing
#     holds a parsed copy of it, and a run that finds a frozen file no longer
#     the one it started on carries no verdict.
#   a registered witness branches. Every function named on a "witness" line is
#     read out of the harness's own source and refused if it files a fact and
#     nothing in its body branches on the receiver or on an argument it was
#     handed.
#   redemption follows a declared relation. Evidence redeems only the mechanism
#     whose registered witness filed it, and an entailment redeems only along an
#     "entailed-by" line above, at matching polarity, with the antecedent
#     redeemed by evidence in that same case.
#
#   None of that refuses a redefinition carried through consistently — rewritten
#   here and in both era peers, or flipped here and in the peer that declared
#   it. That is by design: what this file buys is that the change is legible, in
#   this commit, not that it is impossible.
#
# WHAT REMAINS POSSIBLE, AND FOR WHOM
#
#   What is left is the harness misreporting what it saw, and it is not a list
#   of known holes but the shape of every witness: each one is handed the
#   artifact it judges — a parameter, or a field of the harness's own handle —
#   and in a single-process harness that artifact is a value the caller can
#   build. So every PROVEN cell is reachable from a case body with no process,
#   no socket, and no frozen-file edit:
#
#     (*daemonProc).witnessDrain files an exit as SIGTERM's whenever signalled
#       is set, and signalled is an ordinary field of the harness's own process
#       handle: the witness is callable on a struct literal no daemon ever
#       backed, no exit the OS reaped required, and it passes the branch audit
#       precisely because it branches on that receiver;
#     witnessVerdict and witnessControlTrustGate judge report values their
#       caller decoded — or built;
#     the conformance the proposition and disposition freezes bind is
#       Declaration.JSON, a string the manifest's caller supplies. That each
#       string is a peer process's own output is declaredBy's doing, and
#       declaredBy is harness code like the rest;
#     the class on every filed fact — "a process exit the OS reaped", "bytes
#       the relay copied" — is an EvidenceKind the witness passes as an
#       argument. The witness binding checks (site, mechanism, kind) and never
#       that an artifact of that class exists, so the journal's vocabulary is a
#       label the harness picks — the mechanism under both entries above;
#     a registered witness gutted to a branch that decides nothing — always
#       true, or placed after the filing call, or sitting in an unrelated
#       closure — still passes the branch audit, which walks the body flat with
#       no dominance or ordering analysis. Refusing that needs a decision
#       procedure this gate does not have.
#
#   The boundary that would enclose this class encloses process spawning and
#   socket serving, which is not what a coverage package is — and would not
#   help: the harness would still be the caller reporting what it saw.
#
#   The record is written by the run that produces it, and not by this package
#   alone: scripts/mixed-era.sh exports MIXED_ERA_COVERAGE to the whole
#   ./ci/mixedera/... invocation, so any package in that run can write the
#   release record outside every binding here. Narrowing that export is the
#   script's edit, not this file's. Forming the verdict outside the run is the
#   phase-2 TODO in ci/mixedera/coverage.
#
#   A peer built against the wrong era is caught for the precut peer, whose
#   refusal cases go red the moment the two transports agree; for the cut peer
#   — the threat being a stand-in that never runs the tree's transport — the
#   check reduces to the era string its own conformance declares, compared by
#   scripts/mixed-era.sh at tag time against a record this run wrote.
#
#   Which is the shape of the thing. This gate is built against drift and
#   accident — a case deleted, a run filtered down by -run, a rename that
#   orphans a requirement, a peer accidentally built against the wrong era, an
#   absence quietly dropped, a name repointed at another claim — and not
#   against its own author. A cross-era coverage gate is for the first. Nothing
#   arranged inside one repository is for the second.

mechanism frame-v1
  witness wire (*relay).witness
  era precut claimed
  era cut claimed
  proposition a packet the relay copied carries that era's frozen 6-byte frame identity at the head of its body: the DKS1 magic and the era's own protocol number

mechanism protocol-gate
  witness wire assertCrispRefusal
  witness peer witnessVerdict
  era precut claimed
  era cut claimed
  proposition a handshake between the two eras is promptly refused as a typed protocol mismatch

mechanism session
  witness peer witnessVerdict
  era precut claimed
  era cut claimed
  proposition a client and a daemon at one protocol complete a request and its response over one unix socket

mechanism drain-sigterm
  witness process (*daemonProc).witnessDrain
  era precut claimed
  era cut claimed
  proposition SIGTERM ends the daemon at exit status 0

mechanism drain-preamble
  witness process (*daemonProc).witnessPreamble
  era precut absent
  era cut absent
  proposition a connection whose first bytes are the frozen two-byte drain preamble drains the daemon it reaches

mechanism drain-preamble-emitted
  witness wire assertPreambleAnswered
  era precut absent
  era cut claimed
  proposition a daemon already draining answers a handshake it is still reading with exactly the frozen two-byte preamble and nothing else

mechanism drain-preamble-trust-gate
  era precut absent
  era cut absent
  entailed-by precut drain-preamble
  proposition the drain an inbound frozen preamble admits is still authorized by Trust.Control, the preamble sitting above the trust gate, so an untrusted peer's preamble leaves the incumbent running

mechanism drain-control-trust-gate
  witness peer witnessControlTrustGate
  era precut absent
  era cut claimed
  proposition a drain arriving on the control lane is authorized by Trust.Control: one peer's drain of a daemon whose control lane names a requirement that peer cannot prove is refused untrusted, that daemon still completes the same peer's session at one protocol on the socket it refused the drain from, and that same peer's drain of a daemon naming no control requirement is honoured, reaping the pid of the daemon it stopped
